text:
Priya R: hi all — first day setup issue. my app can't talk to Postgres in docker-compose. postgres service keeps exiting with "could not bind IPv4 socket: Address already in use". i didn't touch ports in compose, using default 5432:5432.
Marcus D: welcome! that error usually means something on the host is already listening on 5432 (homebrew postgres, another container, etc.). run `lsof -iTCP:5432 -sTCP:LISTEN` on your host to check.
Priya R: ran that and it shows /usr/local/opt/postgresql/bin/postgres. i did `brew services list` and it was running.
Elena T: yep — if host postgres is running, docker compose cannot bind host port 5432 and the container will fail to start. two options: 1) stop the host postgres while using the compose stack (`brew services stop postgresql`) or 2) change the host port mapping in docker-compose to avoid conflict, e.g. "5433:5432" so host 5433 -> container 5432.
Ben C: another angle — if your app runs in a container and connects to the postgres service by hostname, use the service name (`postgres`) as the host rather than `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`. localhost inside a container is the container itself.
Priya R: i changed compose to `5433:5432` and compose starts clean. but my app (in another container) still throws `could not connect to server: Connection refused` when using DB_HOST=localhost in .env.
Marcus D: yep that's the localhost vs service name confusion. From inside the app container, `localhost` is the app container. update DB_HOST to the service name (the one in compose, e.g. `postgres`) OR use internal docker network alias. Example `.env` for dev: `DB_HOST=postgres`, `DB_PORT=5432`.
Priya R: ok changed to DB_HOST=postgres, now i see different error: `psql: FATAL: password authentication failed for user "postgres"`. i didn't set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in compose — i thought it would just work.
Elena T: Postgres requires a password if the image is configured that way. In `docker-compose.yml` set env `POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}` (or hardcode for local dev) or use an init file to create users. Also check `pg_hba.conf` auth method if you customize it.
Priya R: i added POSTGRES_PASSWORD in my .env and restarted. psql connects from host if i use port 5433 and the password, but when i `docker-compose exec postgres psql -U postgres` it says "Peer authentication failed".
Ben C: `docker-compose exec postgres psql -U postgres` will try peer auth for local unix sockets. Use `psql -U postgres -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5432` inside the container to force TCP auth with the password, or just use `docker-compose exec -T postgres psql -U postgres -c '\conninfo'` with the right flags. Alternatively, run `psql -U postgres` as the `postgres` user inside the container: `docker-compose exec --user postgres postgres psql`.
Priya R: running `docker-compose exec --user postgres postgres psql` worked and i'm in. thanks. quick follow-up: when i start the stack and then run my test suite from host, it tries to connect to host:5432 and fails — i assume i need to change my local test config to point to 5433 if i kept host port 5433?
Marcus D: correct. If you mapped host 5433 -> container 5432, your host-side tools must connect to 5433. But app containers should talk to `postgres:5432`. For tests running on host, point them to localhost:5433 (or stop host postgres and use 5432).

Elena T: small note on volumes: if you use a persistent volume for `/var/lib/postgresql/data`, permissions can bite (files owned by root). If initdb fails, `sudo chown -R 999:999 ./pgdata` or start the container once without a host mount to let it bootstrap, then reattach.
Priya R: thanks everyone — fixed the port conflict and host vs service naming, tests green now. saved a short checklist in my dotfiles for local dev setup. :sparkles: 
Marcus D: awesome — welcome aboard! also add `.env.local` to .gitignore and don't commit credentials. :lock:
Priya R: will do, thanks again!
